title: September 2019 Class College Final Exam (Part 6 of 6)
unit: Comprehensive Nursing (Medical-Surgical, Paediatrics, Midwifery, Community Health, Mental Health, Pharmacology, Research, Leadership and Management)

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the September 2019 class College Final Exam paper (Kenya Registered Nursing, sat 18 November 2022, Multiple Choice Questions, Q101 to Q120).

questions.text: A true statement regarding Echinococcus granulosus is:

options.B: Transmitted to human via dog licks
options.D: Pruritus ani is a common manifestation

questions.explanation: Transmitted to human via dog licks (B) is correct because Echinococcus granulosus is the dog tapeworm: dogs are the definitive hosts and pass eggs in their faeces, and people become infected by swallowing eggs from contaminated dog fur, licks, hands, food or water, which causes hydatid cysts mainly in the liver and lungs. Transmitted via ingesting undercooked pork (A) is incorrect because that is the route of Taenia solium. Also called beef tape worms (C) is incorrect because the beef tapeworm is Taenia saginata. Pruritus ani is a common manifestation (D) is incorrect because perianal itching is typical of pinworm (Enterobius vermicularis).

questions.text: In TB management, peripheral neuropathy is a complication associated with:
questions.explanation: Isoniazid (D) is correct because isoniazid interferes with vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) metabolism and can cause peripheral neuropathy (numbness and tingling of the hands and feet), which is prevented by giving pyridoxine, especially in HIV, diabetes, malnutrition, alcohol use and pregnancy. Pyrazinamide (A) is incorrect because its main problems are hepatotoxicity, hyperuricaemia and joint pains. Ethambutol (B) is incorrect because it causes optic neuritis, with loss of visual acuity and red-green colour discrimination. Rifampicin (C) is incorrect because it causes orange discolouration of body fluids, hepatitis and drug interactions.

questions.text: Nematodes that have pulmonary migration are:
questions.explanation: Necator americanus, Ascaris lumbricoides (B) is correct because in both species the larvae penetrate the intestine or skin, travel through the blood to the lungs, are coughed up and swallowed, and mature in the small intestine (this lung phase can cause Loeffler's syndrome). Note: the paper's marked key shows D, but this does not agree with standard parasitology because Trichuris trichiura has no lung migration (its larvae develop in the gut wall). Ankylostoma duodenale, Enterobius vermicularis (A) is incorrect because, although hookworm migrates through the lungs, Enterobius does not and develops in the gut. Enterobius vermicularis, Trichuris trichiura (C) is incorrect because neither has a lung phase. Ascaris lumbricoides, Trichuris trichiura (D) is incorrect because only Ascaris has a lung phase.

questions.text: The drug of choice in the management of Shigellosis is:
questions.explanation: Ciprofloxacin (A) is correct because it is the recommended first-line antibiotic for shigellosis (bloody diarrhoea) for a short course, together with ORS and zinc in children. Azithromycin (B) is incorrect because it is an alternative used when resistance or contraindications are present. Doxycycline (C) is incorrect because resistance is widespread and it is not used for shigellosis. Metronidazole (D) is incorrect because it treats amoebiasis, giardiasis and anaerobic infections, not Shigella.

questions.text: In conductive hearing loss, sound in the Weber test is lateralized to:
questions.explanation: Deaf ear (A) is correct because in conductive hearing loss the bone-conducted sound of the tuning fork placed on the midline of the forehead is heard louder in the affected ear, since the ear is not distracted by background noise, and it is also not masked. Normal ear (B) is incorrect because that is the finding in sensorineural hearing loss, where sound goes to the better ear. Both ears (C) is incorrect because it is the normal finding, with sound heard equally in the midline. None of the ear (D) is incorrect because the patient always hears the sound in at least one ear unless there is total deafness in both.

questions.text: In Kenya, a vaccine that is administered once is:
questions.explanation: IPV (B) is the marked answer because at the time of this paper the inactivated polio vaccine was given as a single 0.5 ml intramuscular dose at 14 weeks. OPV (A) is incorrect because it is given in four doses (at birth, 6, 10 and 14 weeks). Rota (C) is incorrect because it is given in three doses (6, 10 and 14 weeks). Pentavalent (D) is incorrect because it is given in three doses (6, 10 and 14 weeks). Note that this is time-sensitive: Kenya added a second IPV dose at 9 months from November 2025, so IPV is now given twice.

questions.text: In BLS, gastric inflation results from:

options.C: Giving the breath over one second
options.D: Lack of creating a good seal between the face and the mask

questions.explanation: Hyperventilation (A) is correct because breaths that are too fast, too forceful or too large push air into the stomach as well as the lungs when the pressure exceeds the opening pressure of the lower oesophageal sphincter, which risks regurgitation and aspiration; each breath should take about one second and make the chest visibly rise. Insufficient volume of breaths (B) is incorrect because a small volume does not inflate the stomach but gives poor ventilation. Giving the breath over one second (C) is incorrect because it is the recommended technique and lowers the risk of gastric inflation. Lack of creating a good seal between the face and the mask (D) is incorrect because a leak causes loss of air and poor ventilation, not stomach inflation.

questions.text: The effects of Oligohydramnios on the fetus include:
questions.explanation: Talipes pedis (A) is correct because with too little amniotic fluid the fetus is compressed in the uterus, causing limb deformities such as talipes (clubfoot), joint contractures, Potter-type facies, pulmonary hypoplasia and cord compression. Neural tube defect (B) is incorrect because it is a developmental defect (folate-related) and is linked to polyhydramnios when the fetus cannot swallow, not a result of low fluid. Hydrocephalus (C) is incorrect because it is a cause or association of polyhydramnios and not an effect of oligohydramnios. Teratoma (D) is incorrect because it is a germ cell tumour with no relation to the amount of amniotic fluid.

questions.text: The hormone produced by the placenta that antagonizes Insulin is:
questions.explanation: Human placenta lactogen (B) is correct because hPL is the main anti-insulin (diabetogenic) hormone of pregnancy: it causes maternal insulin resistance, raising blood glucose so that more glucose and fatty acids are available to the fetus, and it is the reason gestational diabetes can appear in the second and third trimesters. Human chorionic gonadotrophic hormone (A) is incorrect because it maintains the corpus luteum in early pregnancy and is the basis of pregnancy tests. Estrogen (C) is incorrect because it promotes uterine and breast growth. Progesterone (D) is incorrect because it maintains the pregnancy and relaxes smooth muscle, and its effect on insulin is minor compared with hPL.

questions.text: The EDD for a woman whose LMP was 7th January 2022 is:
questions.explanation: 14th October 2022 (C) is correct using Naegele's rule: take the first day of the last menstrual period (7 January 2022), subtract 3 months (7 October) and add 7 days (14 October), then move to the next year, which gives 14 October 2022 (the same as 280 days from the LMP). Note: the paper's marked key shows B, which does not match this calculation. 14th September 2022 (A) is incorrect because it applies the month adjustment wrongly. 1st October 2022 (B) is incorrect because it does not result from Naegele's rule. 7th October 2022 (D) is incorrect because it calculates subtracting 3 months without adding 7 days.

questions.text: Signs of true labor include:

options.A: Urge to bear down, strong uterine action
options.B: Appearance of show, strong uterine action
options.C: Ruptured fetal membranes, gush of fore waters

questions.explanation: Appearance of show, strong uterine action (B) is correct because true labour has regular, increasingly strong and frequent contractions that cause progressive cervical effacement and dilatation, together with a show (blood-stained mucus from the cervix), and the pain is not relieved by walking or rest. Urge to bear down, strong uterine action (A) is incorrect because the urge to push is a sign of the second stage, when the cervix is fully dilated. Ruptured fetal membranes, gush of fore waters (C) is incorrect because membranes may rupture before labour starts or in false labour. Back pains, restlessness (D) is incorrect because they are non-specific and also occur in false labour.

questions.text: The fetal heart rate and uterine action are recorded in the partograph once every:
questions.explanation: 0.5 hour (D) is correct because on the partograph the fetal heart rate and the frequency and duration of contractions are recorded every 30 minutes in the active phase of labour, so that fetal distress and poor progress are picked up early. 4 hours (A) is incorrect because it is the interval for vaginal examination to record cervical dilatation and descent, unless indicated sooner. 2 hours (B) is incorrect because it is too long for monitoring the fetal heart rate and contractions. 1 hour (C) is incorrect because it is also longer than the standard interval.

questions.text: A nursing intervention in 3rd stage of labor, that will prevent post-partum hemorrhage from occurring is:

options.B: Delivering the placenta by pulling on the cord
options.C: Stuffing the birth canal with gauze
options.D: Encouraging ambulation immediately after the end of 3rd stage

questions.explanation: Massaging the uterus (A) is correct because after the placenta is delivered, rubbing up a contraction of the uterus makes the muscle fibres compress the blood vessels (living ligatures) and controls bleeding; it is part of active management of the third stage together with an oxytocic drug and controlled cord traction. Delivering the placenta by pulling on the cord (B) is incorrect because uncontrolled cord traction can cause uterine inversion and haemorrhage. Stuffing the birth canal with gauze (C) is incorrect because it hides bleeding and introduces infection. Encouraging ambulation immediately after the end of 3rd stage (D) is incorrect because the mother must be observed and rested, as early walking risks faintness and bleeding.

questions.text: The drug used to prevent recurrence of puerperal psychosis in subsequent deliveries is:
questions.explanation: Lithium (A) is correct because it is a mood stabiliser used as prophylaxis in women with a history of puerperal (postpartum) psychosis or bipolar disorder, started in late pregnancy or soon after delivery, with the serum lithium level monitored. Haloperidol (B) is incorrect because it is an antipsychotic used to treat an acute episode. Fluphenazine (C) is incorrect because it is a depot antipsychotic used for maintenance treatment of schizophrenia. Largactil (D) is incorrect because chlorpromazine is an antipsychotic used for acute psychosis and agitation, not as prophylaxis.

questions.text: A skin assessment finding, for a patient diagnosed with Psoriasis include:

options.C: Small red scaling patches on the groin

questions.explanation: Thick pitted nails (A) is correct because psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune skin disease with well-defined red plaques covered by silvery scales on the elbows, knees, scalp and back, and nail changes such as pitting, thickening and separation from the nail bed are common. Fluid filled blisters (B) is incorrect because blisters point to conditions such as pemphigus, pemphigoid or burns. Small red scaling patches on the groin (C) is incorrect because they are more typical of fungal infection (tinea cruris) or candidiasis. Brown nodules between the fingers (D) is incorrect because lesions in the finger webs suggest scabies.

questions.text: In theatre, the receiving area nurse would raise a concern if which of the following scenario:

options.B: Patient with a GCS score of 10/15
options.C: Patient with a platelet count of 40,000/mm3
options.D: A 2 year old who took apple juice 2 hours ago

questions.explanation: Patient with a platelet count of 40,000/mm3 (C) is correct because the normal platelet count is 150,000 to 400,000 per mm3, and a count below about 50,000 gives a high risk of bleeding during and after surgery, so the surgeon and anaesthetist must be informed before the operation proceeds. Patient with a Hb of 12.5g/dl (A) is incorrect because it is a normal haemoglobin. Patient with a GCS score of 10/15 (B) is incorrect because it shows altered consciousness that needs monitoring, but it is not on its own a reason to cancel surgery, and it may be the reason for the operation. A 2 year old who took apple juice 2 hours ago (D) is incorrect because clear fluids are generally allowed up to 2 hours before anaesthesia.

questions.text: The range of movement at a hinge joint is:
questions.explanation: Flexion and extension (B) is correct because a hinge joint (such as the elbow, knee, ankle and interphalangeal joints) moves in one plane only, like a door hinge, allowing bending and straightening. Rotation and circumduction (A) is incorrect because they occur at ball-and-socket joints such as the shoulder and hip. Abduction and adduction (C) is incorrect because they occur at ball-and-socket and condyloid joints such as the hip and wrist. Pronation and supination (D) is incorrect because they occur at pivot joints such as the radioulnar joint.

questions.text: Acute hoarseness and stridor immediately post thyroidectomy results from injury to the:
questions.explanation: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (C) is correct because it supplies the muscles of the vocal cords and runs next to the thyroid gland, so it can be bruised or cut during surgery; injury causes hoarseness, and bilateral injury makes the cords come together, causing stridor and airway obstruction, which is an emergency (tracheostomy set kept at the bedside). Vagus nerve (A) is incorrect as the best answer because the recurrent laryngeal nerve is its branch, and the specific nerve at risk is the recurrent laryngeal. Trigeminal nerve (B) is incorrect because it supplies facial sensation and the muscles of chewing. Glossopharyngeal nerve (D) is incorrect because it supplies the pharynx, taste at the back of the tongue and the parotid gland.

questions.text: The effect of sympathetic stimulation to the stomach is:

options.D: Reduces the tone of pyloric sphincter

questions.explanation: Reduces secretion of digestive juices (B) is correct because sympathetic stimulation (fight or flight) diverts blood from the gut, reduces gastric secretions and motility, and contracts sphincters, so digestion slows. Increase muscle tone (A) is incorrect because that is a parasympathetic (vagal) effect. Increases rate of gastric emptying (C) is incorrect because sympathetic activity slows gastric emptying. Reduces the tone of pyloric sphincter (D) is incorrect because sympathetic stimulation increases the tone of the pyloric sphincter.

questions.text: The type of epithelium tissue lining the urinary bladder is:
questions.explanation: Transitional (A) is correct because the bladder is lined by transitional epithelium (urothelium), which has several layers of cells that change shape and flatten as the bladder fills, and it resists the toxic effect of urine. Squamous (B) is incorrect because it lines surfaces such as the skin, mouth and oesophagus, and the alveoli (simple squamous). Columnar (C) is incorrect because it lines the stomach and intestines. Ciliated (D) is incorrect because it lines the respiratory tract and the fallopian tubes to move mucus and ova.
